scope: CM-TERM bounded canonical executable TypedIR -> single ClayVM -> existing CM-13 Linux host-process slice

facts: The retained CM-13 component already owned absolute argv execution with shell=false, bounded stdout/stderr capture, timeout/output-limit handling, clean environment and process-group semantics.
It was outside the canonical ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 -> serialized ClayVM execution path.

canonical_execution_gap: ClayVM already had OP_HOSTCALL and runtime capability checking but compile_typed_ir did not lower a hostcall expression.
The executable IR adapter admitted only the pure Int/Bool overlap and rejected host/effect nodes.
Canonical source/typecheck host intrinsic Clay signatures remain unbound; source-level host intrinsic admission is therefore still open.
observed_reality.concurrency_event: An initial duplicate process-adapter direction was discarded after current main advanced with the CM-13 host-process merge. The retained implementation reuses that component instead of creating a second Linux process runtime.

grf.generated_hypothesis: The highest-information nonduplicate CM-TERM step is to close only the typed/effect IR -> OP_HOSTCALL -> already-canonical CM-13 process boundary while preserving fail-closed capability/effect identity.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: A VM hostcall extension could become a shadow authority channel, silently introduce shell interpretation, duplicate the host-process runtime or falsely look like a full ClayCode process path even though source host signatures and String/Bytes/argv values are absent.
discriminators: Only the named linux.process.spawn.v0 capability maps to the new fixed hostcall ID.
Executable TypedIR must explicitly carry EXTERNAL_COMMUNICATION effect identity for the hostcall.
ClayHost capability denial remains authoritative at runtime.
The VM bridge delegates to the existing CM-13 run_host_process implementation rather than implementing spawn again.
A shell-metacharacter argv decoy must remain literal and produce no shell side effect.
grf.collapse: The bounded TypedIR/VM/process edge is supported and promoted. Full source-level ClayCode process semantics and full CM-TERM remain open.

mechanism: compile_typed_ir admits an explicit integer-argument hostcall bootstrap node and lowers it into the pre-existing OP_HOSTCALL instruction.
ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 adapter admits only linux.process.spawn.v0 for this slice and requires EXTERNAL_COMMUNICATION in both the hostcall node and observed typecheck-effect identity.
HostProcessVMHost maps one integer request handle to an immutable VMProcessRequest and delegates execution to the pre-existing CM-13 run_host_process boundary.
The real process exit status re-enters the VM as Int; captured stdout/stderr remain verification receipts rather than Clay-visible streaming values.

successful_steps: Preserve existing VM and CM-13 regressions
Gate typed effect to real Linux process
exact_head_execution.gate_contract: The workflow exits nonzero on test failure and additionally greps PASS_CM_TERM_TYPED_IR_VM_PROCESS_SLICE plus unusual_experiment_count=1 from the emitted result JSON.
exact_head_execution.raw_log_connector_note: GitHub log download endpoint returned empty content through the available connector; no raw-log details beyond job/step status are invented.

exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment_f.name: SHELL_METACHARACTER_DECOY
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment_f.setup: Pass one argv element containing semicolon, command-substitution syntax and a touch command to /usr/bin/printf through the canonical CM-13 shell=false process boundary; a temporary marker path is embedded in the literal payload.
required_observations: stdout is byte-for-byte the literal payload
the marker file does not exist after execution
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment_f.interpretation: No implicit shell interpretation was observed in the tested path.

external_primary_source_fusion.linux_execve: Linux execve defines explicit path, argv[] and envp[] process-image inputs; this supports keeping argv/environment as explicit typed data rather than a shell command string.
external_primary_source_fusion.linux_pty: Linux PTY documentation defines a master/slave bidirectional terminal channel; PTY semantics are a separate boundary from ordinary pipe-based process execution.
external_primary_source_fusion.python_subprocess: Current Python subprocess documentation recommends sequence args and documents shell=False as the default; current CM-13 implementation already follows this explicit-argv/no-shell shape.
external_primary_source_fusion.architecture_consequence: Keep direct argv execution and PTY/shell as separate explicit capabilities. Do not add shell parsing to the new VM process hostcall.

counterevidence_and_nonclaims: The test constructs the effectful ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 fixture directly; canonical source materialization/typechecking still cannot emit a typed process intrinsic.
Nominal host signatures remain untyped at the Clay language boundary.
ClayVM still lacks canonical String/Bytes/argv/env values and typed function-parameter metadata for those values.
stdout/stderr are receipt bytes only; Clay-visible streaming stdin/stdout/stderr is not implemented.
PTY, explicit shell capability, terminal sizing/modes, signals and cancellation are not implemented by this slice.
No full CM-TERM baseline PASS is claimed.
No whole Clay Machine acceptance is claimed.

cross_frontier_fusion.constraint: Do not widen VM values ad hoc. CM-DATA and CM-TERM should converge on an explicit typed value/module-format/runtime admission contract for String/Bytes/argv/buffer semantics with provenance and fail-closed type admission.
cross_frontier_fusion.next_falsifier: Design the smallest explicitly typed/versioned ClayVM value boundary that can carry one owned immutable Bytes/String argv value from canonical source/typecheck into ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 and the single VM. Prove wrong-type admission fails, process argv remains literal, and the same value contract can be reused by CM-DATA. Only after that add Clay-visible streaming byte channels; treat PTY as a separate explicit channel/capability.
